prompt: Which is lighter, a big balloon or a small rock?
explanation: Big things are not always heavy. A balloon is full of air, so it is lighter than a rock.

prompt: When do you eat breakfast?
explanation: Breakfast is the first meal of the day, so we eat it in the morning.

prompt: Which takes longer, sleeping at night or brushing your teeth?
explanation: Brushing your teeth takes a few minutes. Sleeping takes all night, so it takes longer.

prompt: Mia went to the beach the day before today. When did she go?
explanation: The day before today is called yesterday.

prompt: What do you put on first, your socks or your shoes?
explanation: Your socks go on first, then your shoes go on over them.

prompt: How many days are there in one week?
explanation: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. That is 7 days.

prompt: What day comes after Monday?
explanation: The days go Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. Tuesday comes after Monday.

prompt: What day comes just before Friday?
explanation: The days go Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. Thursday is just before Friday.

prompt: Today is Sunday. What day will it be tomorrow?
explanation: After Sunday the week starts again with Monday. Saturday was yesterday.

explanation: One more than 99 is 100. After 99 we start a new hundred.

prompt: What number comes just after 34?
explanation: Counting on from 34: 34, 35. So 35 comes next.

prompt: What number comes just before 27?
explanation: Counting back from 27: 27, 26. So 26 comes just before.

prompt: Count back: 112, 111, 110, ___. What number comes next?
explanation: One less than 110 is 109. The tens go back from 11 tens to 10 tens and 9 ones.

prompt: Which is the same as 63?
explanation: In 63 the 6 means 6 tens (sixty) and the 3 means 3 ones.

prompt: Which number is the smallest?
explanation: 17 has only 1 ten. 27 has 2 tens and 71 has 7 tens, so 17 is the smallest.

prompt: Which list goes from smallest to biggest?
explanation: 19 is less than 91, and 91 is less than 109. So the order is 19, 91, 109.

prompt: Which one is a flat 2D shape, not a 3D object?
explanation: A square is flat. A cube, a cone and a sphere are 3D objects you can pick up.

prompt: I have 2 flat faces that are circles. I can roll. What am I?
explanation: A cylinder, like a can, has a circle at each end and a curved surface, so it rolls. A cone has only 1 circle face.

figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 212" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="192" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M130 10v192M250 10v192M10 74h360M10 138h360"/><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="17" text-anchor="middle"><text x="70" y="48">Park</text><text x="190" y="48">School</text><text x="310" y="48">Pool</text><text x="70" y="112">Shop</text><text x="190" y="112">Home</text><text x="310" y="112">Bakery</text><text x="70" y="176">Beach</text><text x="190" y="176">Library</text><text x="310" y="176">Farm</text></g></svg>
explanation: 1 square down from Home is the Library. 1 square left from there is the Beach.

prompt: Which path goes from the Shop to the Pool?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 212" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="192" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M130 10v192M250 10v192M10 74h360M10 138h360"/><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="17" text-anchor="middle"><text x="70" y="48">Park</text><text x="190" y="48">School</text><text x="310" y="48">Pool</text><text x="70" y="112">Shop</text><text x="190" y="112">Home</text><text x="310" y="112">Bakery</text><text x="70" y="176">Beach</text><text x="190" y="176">Library</text><text x="310" y="176">Farm</text></g></svg>
explanation: From the Shop, go up 1 to the Park, then right 2 past the School to the Pool.

explanation: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 7, so it is 7 centimetres long.

prompt: Which would you measure in metres?
explanation: A classroom is long, so metres are best. The others are small, so we use centimetres.

prompt: Max's rope is 1 metre long. Ana's rope is 80 centimetres long. How many centimetres longer is Max's rope?
explanation: 1 metre is 100 centimetres. 100 - 80 = 20.

prompt: The ribbon starts at 3 and ends at 9 on the ruler. How many centimetres long is it?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 125" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><rect x="10" y="70" width="460" height="50" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M20 70v18M64 70v18M108 70v18M152 70v18M196 70v18M240 70v18M284 70v18M328 70v18M372 70v18M416 70v18M460 70v18M42 70v10M86 70v10M130 70v10M174 70v10M218 70v10M262 70v10M306 70v10M350 70v10M394 70v10M438 70v10" stroke-width="1.5"/><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle"><text x="20" y="108">0</text><text x="64" y="108">1</text><text x="108" y="108">2</text><text x="152" y="108">3</text><text x="196" y="108">4</text><text x="240" y="108">5</text><text x="284" y="108">6</text><text x="328" y="108">7</text><text x="372" y="108">8</text><text x="416" y="108">9</text><text x="460" y="108">10</text></g><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="13" text-anchor="end"><text x="462" y="64">cm</text></g><rect x="152" y="32" width="264" height="18" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".4"/><path d="M152 54v16M416 54v16" stroke-dasharray="3 3" stroke-width="1.5"/></svg>
explanation: Count the centimetres from 3 to 9: that is 6 centimetres. It is not 9, because it does not start at 0.

prompt: The flag moved from Before to After. Was it a slide, a flip or a turn?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 125" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle"><text x="60" y="115">Before</text><text x="230" y="115">After</text></g><path d="M50 85V15l36 13l-36 13" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M220 85V15l36 13l-36 13" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M110 50h70m-10 -7l10 7l-10 7" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/></svg>
explanation: The flag still points the same way. It just moved across, so it is a slide.

prompt: This flag moved from Before to After. Did it slide, flip or turn?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 125" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle"><text x="60" y="115">Before</text><text x="230" y="115">After</text></g><path d="M50 85V15l36 13l-36 13" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M250 85V15l-36 13l36 13" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M110 50h70m-10 -7l10 7l-10 7" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/></svg>
explanation: The flag now points the other way, like in a mirror, so it is a flip.

prompt: The minute hand makes a quarter turn. How many minutes go by?
explanation: A full turn of the minute hand is 60 minutes. A quarter of that is 15 minutes.

prompt: The arrow pointed up. Now it points right. What turn did it make?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 140" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><path d="M60 95V25m-14 16l14 -16l14 16" stroke-width="4"/><path d="M195 60h70m-16 -14l16 14l-16 14" stroke-width="4"/><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle"><text x="60" y="128">Before</text><text x="230" y="128">After</text></g></svg>
explanation: Turning from up to right goes the same way as clock hands, a quarter of the way round. That is a quarter turn clockwise.

prompt: Which shape has 5 straight sides?
explanation: A pentagon has 5 straight sides.

prompt: Which shape has no straight sides?
explanation: A circle has one curved side and no straight sides.

prompt: Which shape has sides that are parallel?
explanation: A rectangle's opposite sides always stay the same distance apart, so they are parallel.

prompt: Two triangles are joined along their long sides, like this. What shape do they make?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 220 120" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><path d="M20 20h180v80H20z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M20 100L200 20"/></svg>
explanation: The joined shape has 4 straight sides and 4 square corners, and it is longer than it is tall. It is a rectangle.

prompt: This rectangle is covered with squares. How many squares are there?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 180 140" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><rect x="10" y="10" width="160" height="120" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M50 10v120M90 10v120M130 10v120M10 50h160M10 90h160"/></svg>
explanation: There are 3 rows of 4 squares. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

prompt: Count the squares. Which shape has the bigger area?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 410 140" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><rect x="10" y="50" width="238" height="34" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M44 50v34M78 50v34M112 50v34M146 50v34M180 50v34M214 50v34"/><rect x="290" y="16" width="102" height="102" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M324 16v102M358 16v102M290 50h102M290 84h102"/><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold"><text x="129" y="120">Shape A</text><text x="341" y="135">Shape B</text></g></svg>
explanation: Shape A covers 7 squares. Shape B covers 9 squares, so Shape B has the bigger area.

prompt: Lily covers a table with big tiles. Tom covers the same table with small tiles. Who uses more tiles?
explanation: Small tiles cover less each, so Tom needs more of them to cover the same table.

prompt: A rectangle is covered by 5 rows of squares. Each row has 4 squares. How many squares are there?
How many faces does a cube have?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 150" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><path d="M20 50h80v80H20z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M20 50L56 18H136L100 50Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".05"/><path d="M100 50L136 18V98L100 130Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".3"/><path d="M20 130l36 -32h80M56 98V18" stroke-dasharray="5 4" stroke-width="1.5"/></svg>
explanation: A cube has a top, a bottom and 4 sides. That is 6 faces.

prompt: What shape is each face of a cube?
explanation: Every face of a cube is a square.

prompt: How many vertices (corners) does a cube have?
explanation: A cube has 4 corners on the top and 4 on the bottom. That is 8 vertices.

prompt: A cereal box is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
explanation: It has 4 edges on the top, 4 on the bottom and 4 going up the sides. That is 12.

prompt: The jug holds 8 cups. The bottle holds 3 cups. The bowl holds 5 cups. Which holds the most?
explanation: 8 cups is more than 5 or 3, so the jug holds the most.

prompt: A bucket holds 10 cups. A mug holds 1 cup. Which holds less?
explanation: 1 cup is less than 10 cups, so the mug holds less.

prompt: A vase holds 6 cups, a pot 9 cups, a glass 2 cups. Which order goes from least to most?
explanation: 2 is the least, then 6, then 9: glass, vase, pot.

prompt: A glass holds about 1 cup of water. Which of these also holds about 1 cup?
explanation: A mug is about the same size as a glass, so it holds about 1 cup. A bath and a bucket hold many cups.

prompt: Model A has 9 cubes. Model B has 12 of the same cubes. Which has the bigger volume?
explanation: 12 cubes is more than 9 cubes, so Model B takes up more space.

prompt: This model is made from cubes in one layer. How many cubes are there?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 154 154" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><rect x="10" y="104" width="40" height="40" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><rect x="10" y="64" width="40" height="40" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><rect x="10" y="24" width="40" height="40" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M10 24l14 -12h40l-14 12z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".05"/><path d="M50 24l14 -12v40l-14 12z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".3"/><rect x="50" y="104" width="40" height="40" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><rect x="50" y="64" width="40" height="40" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M50 64l14 -12h40l-14 12z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".05"/><path d="M90 64l14 -12v40l-14 12z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".3"/><rect x="90" y="104" width="40" height="40" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M90 104l14 -12h40l-14 12z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".05"/><path d="M130 104l14 -12v40l-14 12z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".3"/></svg>
explanation: The steps have 3, 2 and 1 cubes. 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

prompt: Ali builds a tall tower with 8 cubes. Bo builds a flat wall with 8 cubes. Which has more volume?
explanation: Both use 8 of the same cubes, so they have the same volume, even though the shapes are different.

prompt: Jess builds a model with 10 big cubes. Raj builds the same model with small cubes. Who uses more cubes?
explanation: Small cubes take up less space each, so Raj needs more of them to make the same model.

prompt: The apple balances these cubes. How many cubes is the mass of the apple?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 130" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><path d="M150 70l-18 50h36z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><path d="M40 70h220M60 70v-10h0M240 70v-10"/><path d="M20 60h80M200 60h80" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="60" cy="38" r="20" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".25"/><path d="M60 18q2 -8 8 -10"/><rect x="210" y="41" width="18" height="18" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><rect x="231" y="41" width="18" height="18" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><rect x="252" y="41" width="18" height="18" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><rect x="210" y="20" width="18" height="18" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><rect x="231" y="20" width="18" height="18" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/><rect x="252" y="20" width="18" height="18" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".15"/></svg>
explanation: There are 6 cubes on the other side and the scale is level, so the apple is as heavy as 6 cubes.

prompt: The book balances 12 marbles. The cup balances 8 marbles. Which is heavier?
explanation: 12 marbles is more than 8 marbles, so the book is heavier.

prompt: Kim squashes a ball of play dough into a long snake. What happens to its mass?
explanation: No dough was added or taken away, so the mass stays the same.

prompt: A shoe balances 15 cubes. A sock balances 3 cubes. How many more cubes does the shoe balance?
explanation: 15 - 3 = 12 more cubes.

prompt: What time is on this clock?
explanation: The minute hand is on 6, so it is half past. The hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4, so it is half past 3.

prompt: What time does the clock show?
explanation: The minute hand is on 3, so it is quarter past. The hour hand is just past 7, so it is quarter past 7.

prompt: At half past 5, where does the hour hand point?
explanation: At half past 5 the hour hand has gone halfway from 5 to 6.

prompt: Which digital time matches this clock?
explanation: The minute hand is on 9, which is 45 minutes. The hour hand is nearly at 11, so it is quarter to 11, or 10:45.

prompt: Look at the calendar. What day of the week is 12 November?

explanation: Find 12 on the calendar and look up to the top of its column: Thu, which is Thursday.

prompt: Which is the longest?
explanation: 1 hour is 60 minutes, and 1 minute is 60 seconds, so 1 hour is the longest.

prompt: Today is 5 November. Ty's party is on 19 November. How many days until the party?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 328 232" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="17" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold"><text x="164.0" y="22">November</text></g><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold"><text x="32" y="48">Mon</text><text x="76" y="48">Tue</text><text x="120" y="48">Wed</text><text x="164" y="48">Thu</text><text x="208" y="48">Fri</text><text x="252" y="48">Sat</text><text x="296" y="48">Sun</text></g><path d="M10 56h308M10 84h308M10 112h308M10 140h308M10 168h308M10 196h308M10 224h308M10 56v168M54 56v168M98 56v168M142 56v168M186 56v168M230 56v168M274 56v168M318 56v168" stroke-width="1"/><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle"><text x="296" y="75">1</text><text x="32" y="103">2</text><text x="76" y="103">3</text><text x="120" y="103">4</text><text x="164" y="103">5</text><text x="208" y="103">6</text><text x="252" y="103">7</text><text x="296" y="103">8</text><text x="32" y="131">9</text><text x="76" y="131">10</text><text x="120" y="131">11</text><text x="164" y="131">12</text><text x="208" y="131">13</text><text x="252" y="131">14</text><text x="296" y="131">15</text><text x="32" y="159">16</text><text x="76" y="159">17</text><text x="120" y="159">18</text><text x="164" y="159">19</text><text x="208" y="159">20</text><text x="252" y="159">21</text><text x="296" y="159">22</text><text x="32" y="187">23</text><text x="76" y="187">24</text><text x="120" y="187">25</text><text x="164" y="187">26</text><text x="208" y="187">27</text><text x="252" y="187">28</text><text x="296" y="187">29</text><text x="32" y="215">30</text></g></svg>

prompt: Dad goes away on 2 November and comes home on 23 November. How many weeks is he away?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 328 232" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" font-family="sans-serif"><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="17" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold"><text x="164.0" y="22">November</text></g><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold"><text x="32" y="48">Mon</text><text x="76" y="48">Tue</text><text x="120" y="48">Wed</text><text x="164" y="48">Thu</text><text x="208" y="48">Fri</text><text x="252" y="48">Sat</text><text x="296" y="48">Sun</text></g><path d="M10 56h308M10 84h308M10 112h308M10 140h308M10 168h308M10 196h308M10 224h308M10 56v168M54 56v168M98 56v168M142 56v168M186 56v168M230 56v168M274 56v168M318 56v168" stroke-width="1"/><g fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle"><text x="296" y="75">1</text><text x="32" y="103">2</text><text x="76" y="103">3</text><text x="120" y="103">4</text><text x="164" y="103">5</text><text x="208" y="103">6</text><text x="252" y="103">7</text><text x="296" y="103">8</text><text x="32" y="131">9</text><text x="76" y="131">10</text><text x="120" y="131">11</text><text x="164" y="131">12</text><text x="208" y="131">13</text><text x="252" y="131">14</text><text x="296" y="131">15</text><text x="32" y="159">16</text><text x="76" y="159">17</text><text x="120" y="159">18</text><text x="164" y="159">19</text><text x="208" y="159">20</text><text x="252" y="159">21</text><text x="296" y="159">22</text><text x="32" y="187">23</text><text x="76" y="187">24</text><text x="120" y="187">25</text><text x="164" y="187">26</text><text x="208" y="187">27</text><text x="252" y="187">28</text><text x="296" y="187">29</text><text x="32" y="215">30</text></g></svg>

prompt: Look at the picture graph. Which fruit did the most children choose?

say: What fraction is missing to make one whole? Three quarters plus blank equals one.
explanation: 4 quarters make a whole. 3 quarters and 1 more quarter make 4 quarters, so 1/4 is missing.

prompt: How many thirds make one whole?
explanation: A whole split into thirds has 3 equal parts, so 3 thirds make one whole.

prompt: Grace has painted 2/5 of a fence. What fraction of the fence does she still need to paint?
say: Grace has painted two fifths of a fence. What fraction of the fence does she still need to paint?
explanation: The whole fence is 5 fifths. 5 fifths − 2 fifths = 3 fifths, so 3/5 is left.

say: A piece of ribbon is 4 centimetres long. It is one third of the whole ribbon. How many centimetres long is the whole ribbon?
explanation: 3 thirds make the whole, so the whole is 3 pieces of 4 cm: 3 × 4 = 12 cm.

explanation: A full school bag is like about three 1 kg bags of flour, so about 3 kg. 30 kg is about as heavy as a Year 3 child.

prompt: Which container holds more than 1 litre?
explanation: A bucket holds many litres. A teaspoon, a cup and a small juice box hold less than 1 litre.

prompt: Which container holds less than 1 litre?
explanation: A coffee mug holds much less than a 1 litre milk carton. The others hold many litres.

prompt: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
explanation: An hour is 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 15.

prompt: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
explanation: There are 60 minutes in one hour.

prompt: Which unit is best for measuring how long it takes to eat a sandwich?
explanation: Eating a sandwich takes a few minutes.

prompt: How many hours are in 2 days?
explanation: One day has 24 hours, so 2 days have 24 + 24 = 48 hours.

prompt: Four friends read for a while. Ali read for 1 hour, Bec for 50 minutes, Cam for 75 minutes and Dev for half an hour. Who read for the longest?
explanation: 1 hour is 60 minutes and half an hour is 30 minutes. 75 minutes is the longest, so Cam read the longest.

prompt: I have 4 straight sides. Only one pair of my sides is parallel. What shape am I?
explanation: A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides. Squares, rectangles and rhombuses have two pairs.

prompt: All four sides of this shape are the same length. It has no right angles. What is it called?

explanation: A shape with four equal sides is a rhombus. It is not a square because it has no right angles.

prompt: This shape has 4 right angles. Its opposite sides are equal, but it is not a square. What is it called?

explanation: A rectangle has 4 right angles and opposite sides of equal length.

prompt: Which shape has two pairs of parallel sides but no right angles?
explanation: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides and its corners are not right angles. A rectangle has right angles.

prompt: This is a square-based pyramid. The dashed lines are edges you cannot see. How many faces does it have?

prompt: A can of baked beans is shaped like which object?
explanation: A can has two flat circle faces and one curved surface, so it is a cylinder.

prompt: Which object has a square base and four triangle faces that meet at a point?
explanation: A pyramid has triangle faces that meet at a point. With a square base it is a square-based pyramid.

prompt: This is a triangular prism. The dashed lines are edges you cannot see. How many edges does it have?

prompt: A bag has 9 red marbles and 1 blue marble. Sam takes one marble without looking. How likely is it that he takes a red marble?
explanation: Most of the marbles are red, so red is likely. It is not certain, because he could take the blue one.

prompt: How likely is it that the sun will rise tomorrow morning?
explanation: The sun rises every morning, so it is certain.

prompt: You roll a normal dice with the numbers 1 to 6. How likely is it that you roll a 7?
explanation: There is no 7 on the dice, so rolling a 7 is impossible.

prompt: You toss a coin. What are all the possible outcomes?
explanation: A coin can land on heads or on tails, so there are 2 possible outcomes.

prompt: You roll a normal dice with the numbers 1 to 6. How many different numbers could you roll?
explanation: The dice could land on 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6. That is 6 outcomes.

prompt: Jo tosses a coin 20 times. About how many heads should she expect?
explanation: Heads and tails are equally likely, so about half of the 20 tosses, about 10, should be heads.

prompt: Ravi predicted 10 heads in 20 coin tosses. He got 13 heads. What is the best way to explain this?

choices.text: Real results are often a bit different from a prediction
Heads always comes up more than tails

prompt: Write forty-six thousand, two hundred and eight as a number.
explanation: Forty-six thousand is 46 000, then add 208 to get 46 208. There are no tens, so the tens digit is 0.

prompt: What is the value of the 7 in 372 615?
explanation: The 7 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 70 000.

prompt: Write 300 000 + 50 000 + 400 + 9 as one number.
explanation: There are 3 hundred thousands, 5 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones: 350 409.

prompt: Which number is the largest?
explanation: All start with 6. 680 thousand is more than 608 thousand, and 680 314 has 3 hundreds, which beats 680 143 with 1 hundred.

prompt: What is 47 × 100?
explanation: Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 47 becomes 4700.

prompt: 4 × 3 = 12. Use this to work out 4 × 30.
explanation: 30 is 3 tens, so 4 × 30 is 12 tens, which is 120.

prompt: What is 3500 ÷ 100?
explanation: Dividing by 100 moves each digit two places to the right, so 3500 becomes 35.

prompt: Pencils come in boxes of 100. How many boxes hold 4800 pencils altogether?
explanation: 4800 is 48 hundreds, so 48 boxes of 100 hold 4800 pencils.

prompt: Which of these numbers is even?
explanation: Only the last digit matters. 51 384 ends in 4, which is even.

prompt: Which of these numbers is odd?
explanation: 40 715 ends in 5, which is odd. The others end in 6, 0 and 8, which are even.

prompt: Ava adds two odd numbers together. What kind of answer will she get?
explanation: Odd + odd is always even, for example 3 + 5 = 8 and 7 + 9 = 16.

prompt: Without working out the answers, which one will be odd?
explanation: Odd × odd is always odd, so 51 × 13 is odd. Odd + odd, even × odd and even + even all give even answers.

prompt: Which decimal is the same as 3/10?
explanation: 3/10 means 3 tenths. The first place after the decimal point is tenths, so it is 0.3.

prompt: How many tenths make one whole?
explanation: One whole split into 10 equal parts gives 10 tenths, so 10/10 = 1.0.

prompt: This number line goes from 0 to 2. Each whole is split into tenths. What number is the arrow pointing to?
explanation: The arrow is 4 small steps past 1, and each step is one tenth, so it points to 1.4.

prompt: Mia has 13 tenths. Write this amount as a decimal.
explanation: 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 13 tenths is 1 whole and 3 tenths: 1.3.

prompt: Which decimal shows 27 hundredths?
explanation: 27 hundredths is 27/100. Hundredths fill two places after the decimal point, so it is 0.27.

prompt: In the number 3.45, what is the value of the 4?
explanation: The first digit after the decimal point is tenths, so the 4 is worth 4 tenths (0.4).

prompt: Which decimal is equal to 0.5?
explanation: 0.5 is 5 tenths, which is the same as 50 hundredths, 0.50. A zero on the end does not change the value.

prompt: Which decimal has 4 tenths and 3 hundredths?
explanation: Tenths come first after the decimal point, then hundredths, so 4 tenths and 3 hundredths is 0.43.

prompt: Which number is bigger: 0.4 or 0.35?
explanation: 0.4 is the same as 0.40, which is 40 hundredths. That is more than 35 hundredths.

prompt: Which decimal is the smallest?
explanation: 0.09 has 0 tenths, and all the others have some tenths, so 0.09 is the smallest.

prompt: Which list of decimals is in order from smallest to largest?
explanation: Compare tenths first: 0.25 has 2 tenths, 0.3 has 3 tenths and 0.7 has 7 tenths.

prompt: Which number is between 0.6 and 0.7?
explanation: 0.6 is 60 hundredths and 0.7 is 70 hundredths. 0.65 is 65 hundredths, which is between them.

prompt: 1/2 = ___/4. What number goes in the gap?
explanation: Quarters are half the size of halves, so you need 2 quarters to make one half: 1/2 = 2/4.

prompt: 1/5 = ___/10. What number goes in the gap?
explanation: Each fifth splits into 2 tenths, so 1/5 = 2/10.

prompt: Sam ate 1/2 of a small pizza. Jo ate 1/2 of a large pizza. Who ate more pizza?
explanation: Half of a bigger whole is bigger, so Jo ate more. Fractions only compare fairly when the wholes are the same size.

prompt: 6/8 = ___/4. What number goes in the gap?
explanation: Every 2 eighths make 1 quarter, so 6 eighths make 3 quarters: 6/8 = 3/4.

prompt: Which decimal is the same as 1/2?
explanation: One half is 5 tenths, so 1/2 = 0.5.

prompt: Which decimal is the same as 7/100?
explanation: 7 hundredths has 0 tenths and 7 hundredths, so it is 0.07.

prompt: Which decimal is the same as 3/4?
explanation: 1/4 = 0.25, so 3/4 is 3 lots of 0.25, which is 0.75.

prompt: Ella's ribbon is 1 1/2 m long. How should she write this length as a decimal?
Count by quarters: 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, ___. What comes next?
explanation: Each step adds one quarter, so after 4/4 comes 5/4, which is the same as 1 1/4.

prompt: What whole number is the same as 5/5?
explanation: 5 fifths make one whole, so 5/5 = 1.

prompt: This number line goes from 0 to 2. Each whole is split into thirds. What fraction is the arrow pointing to?
explanation: Each small step is one third. The arrow is 4 steps from 0, so it shows 4/3, which is 1 1/3.

explanation: 20 + 15 = 35, and 30 + 5 = 35, so the missing number is 5.

explanation: You can add numbers in any order, so 18 + 7 = 7 + 18.

explanation: 1998 is 2 less than 2000, and 3000 − 2000 = 1000, so the answer is 1000 + 2 = 1002.

prompt: Round 3478 to the nearest hundred.
explanation: 3478 is between 3400 and 3500. The tens digit is 7, so it rounds up to 3500.

prompt: Round 2735 to the nearest ten.
explanation: 2735 is exactly halfway between 2730 and 2740. When the ones digit is 5 we round up, so it is 2740.

prompt: Kai buys items costing $4.95, $3.10 and $6.89. Round each to the nearest dollar. Which is the best estimate of the total?
explanation: $4.95 is about $5, $3.10 is about $3 and $6.89 is about $7. 5 + 3 + 7 = 15, so about $15.

prompt: Noah works out 2987 + 4012 and gets 6099. Round each number to the nearest thousand. What should the answer be close to?
explanation: 2987 is about 3000 and 4012 is about 4000, so the answer should be about 7000. Noah's 6099 must be wrong.

explanation: Two sausage rolls cost 2 × $3.50 = $7.00. Add the juice: $7.00 + $2.20 = $9.20.

Pencils cost $2 each. Mei buys 4 pencils and pays with a $10 note. How many dollars of change does she get?
explanation: 4 pencils cost 4 × $2 = $8, and $10 − $8 = $2 change.

prompt: Four friends share the cost of a $30 pizza and $6 of drinks equally. How many dollars does each friend pay?
explanation: Altogether it costs $30 + $6 = $36. Shared between 4 friends: $36 ÷ 4 = $9 each.

prompt: What is 7 × 8?

prompt: Each layer of a prism has 5 cubes. The prism has 3 layers. How many cubes are there altogether?
explanation: 3 layers of 5 cubes is 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 cubes.

prompt: A box is filled with centimetre cubes. It is 4 cubes long, 3 cubes wide and 2 layers high. What is its volume in cubic centimetres?
explanation: One layer has 4 × 3 = 12 cubes. Two layers have 24 cubes, so the volume is 24 cubic centimetres.

prompt: Model A is 3 cubes long, 3 cubes wide and 1 layer high. Model B is 2 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 2 layers high. Which model has the larger volume?
explanation: Model A has 3 × 3 = 9 cubes. Model B has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes in each layer, so 8 cubes. 9 is more than 8.

prompt: The clock shows the time Ben eats breakfast in the morning. Which time is it?
explanation: The long hand points to 9, which is 45 minutes. The short hand is between 7 and 8, so it is 7:45, and morning is am.

explanation: pm times are after midday, so 3:20 pm is in the afternoon. The am times are all in the morning.

prompt: It is 4:35 pm. How many minutes is it until 5:00 pm?
explanation: There are 60 minutes in an hour, and 60 − 35 = 25 minutes.

prompt: Swimming starts at 10:40 am and finishes at 12:15 pm on the same day. How many minutes long is it?
explanation: From 10:40 to 11:00 is 20 minutes, 11:00 to 12:00 is 60 minutes, and 12:00 to 12:15 is 15 minutes: 20 + 60 + 15 = 95 minutes.

choices.text: A list of 30 names with each pet written beside it
A column graph with one column for each pet

explanation: In a column graph the tallest column shows the most popular pet straight away.
verify: 'A column graph with one column for each pet'

prompt: Which set of categories would work best for a survey about how students travel to school?
explanation: Walk, car, bus, bike and other are all ways to travel, and 'other' catches any answer left over.

prompt: The class votes are 23, 27 and 18. They are shown in a table and in a picture graph where one symbol stands for 5 votes. Which display shows the exact numbers more clearly?

choices.text: Both show the exact numbers equally clearly

explanation: With one symbol for 5 votes, 23 or 27 needs part symbols that are hard to read. The table shows the exact numbers.

prompt: A spinner has 8 equal parts: 4 red, 3 blue and 1 green. Which list goes from least likely to most likely?
explanation: Green has 1 part, blue has 3 parts and red has 4 parts, so green is least likely and red is most likely.

prompt: A bag has 9 yellow counters and 1 purple counter. You pick one without looking. Which colour are you more likely to pick?
explanation: There are many more yellow counters than purple ones, so yellow is more likely.

prompt: A spinner has 6 equal parts. 5 parts are blue and 1 part is red. Which word best describes spinning red?
explanation: Only 1 of the 6 parts is red, so red can happen but it is unlikely.

prompt: A spinner has 4 equal parts: 2 red, 1 blue and 1 yellow. Ari predicts red will come up about half the time. He spins 40 times. Which result is closest to his prediction?
explanation: Half of 40 is 20. Red 21 times is very close to 20. Results vary a little, so it is rarely exactly 20.

prompt: Ella tosses a fair coin and gets heads 4 times in a row. What is the chance of heads on the next toss?
explanation: The coin does not remember earlier tosses. Heads and tails are still equally likely on every toss.

prompt: A bag has 2 green marbles and 3 white marbles. Zoe takes out a green marble and does not put it back. How many green marbles are left in the bag?
explanation: There were 2 green marbles and Zoe took 1 out, so 1 green marble is left.

prompt: A bag has 3 red and 3 blue marbles. Jack takes out a red marble, then puts it back. He picks again. Which is true?

choices.text: Red and blue are equally likely

explanation: The marble went back, so the bag still has 3 red and 3 blue. The chances are the same as before.

prompt: A bag has 3 red and 3 blue marbles. Jack takes out a red marble and does NOT put it back. He picks again. Which is true?

choices.text: Red and blue are equally likely

explanation: Now the bag has 2 red and 3 blue marbles, so blue is more likely on the next pick.

prompt: Write four million, three hundred and six thousand, two hundred and fifteen as a numeral.
explanation: Four million is 4 000 000, three hundred and six thousand is 306 000 and then 215, so the number is 4 306 215. The 0 holds the ten thousands place.

prompt: How many thousands make one million?
explanation: 1 000 000 ÷ 1000 = 1000, so one thousand thousands make one million.

prompt: Which of these numbers is the largest? Type it in. 3 099 999, 3 909 000, 3 990 000, 3 900 990
say: Which of these numbers is the largest? Type it in. 3,099,999. 3,909,000. 3,990,000. 3,900,990.
explanation: All four numbers have 3 millions. Next compare the hundred thousands: 0, 9, 9, 9. Then the ten thousands: 3 990 000 has 9, the others have 0, so 3 990 000 is the largest.

say: Fill the gap. 3,450,000 equals 2,000,000 plus what, plus 50,000?
explanation: 3 450 000 − 2 000 000 − 50 000 = 1 400 000. This is a non-standard way to split the number.

prompt: Round 46 382 to the nearest thousand.
say: Round 46,382 to the nearest thousand.
explanation: 46 382 is between 46 000 and 47 000. The hundreds digit is 3, which is less than 5, so it rounds down to 46 000.

prompt: Round 7652 to the nearest hundred.
explanation: 7652 is between 7600 and 7700. The tens digit is 5, so it rounds up to 7700.

prompt: Which is the best estimate of 498 + 312?
explanation: 498 is about 500 and 312 is about 300, so the answer is about 500 + 300 = 800.

prompt: Mia worked out 61 × 49 and got 1989. Which of these is true?

choices.text: Her answer cannot be right, because 60 × 50 = 3000.
Her answer cannot be right, because 60 × 50 = 300.
Her answer is too big, because 61 × 49 is about 1000.

explanation: Rounding gives 60 × 50 = 3000, so 1989 is far too small. (The real answer is 2989.)

prompt: How many factors does 24 have?
explanation: The factor pairs of 24 are 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6, so the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24. That is 8 factors.

prompt: Which number is a factor of 36?
explanation: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 with nothing left over, so 9 is a factor of 36.

prompt: Which number is a multiple of 7?
explanation: 7 × 8 = 56, so 56 is a multiple of 7. Having a 7 in it, like 27 or 47, does not make a number a multiple of 7.

prompt: Which number is divisible by 3?
explanation: A number is divisible by 3 when its digits add to a multiple of 3. For 714, 7 + 1 + 4 = 12, and 12 is a multiple of 3.

prompt: Write 7 thousandths as a decimal.
explanation: Thousandths are the third place after the decimal point, so 7 thousandths is 0.007.

prompt: In the number 4.235, what is the value of the digit 3?
explanation: In 4.235 the 2 is in the tenths place, the 3 is in the hundredths place and the 5 is in the thousandths place. So the 3 is worth 3 hundredths, or 0.03.
5.208 has 5 ones, 2 tenths, 0 hundredths and 8 thousandths, so the missing part is 0.008.

prompt: Write 2 ones, 4 tenths and 15 thousandths as one decimal number.
Which decimal is the largest?
explanation: Compare the tenths first: 0.5 has 5 tenths, and the others have only 3 or 4 tenths. More digits does not mean a bigger number.

prompt: Which decimal is equal to 0.4?
explanation: 0.4 is 4 tenths, and 0.40 is 40 hundredths, which is the same amount. Adding a zero at the end does not change the value.

prompt: Which list of decimals is in order from smallest to largest?
explanation: Write them with three places: 1.205, 1.250, 1.300. Now it is easy to see 1.205 < 1.25 < 1.3.

prompt: Which decimal is equal to 10%?
explanation: 10% is 10/100, which is 1/10, and 1/10 written as a decimal is 0.1.

prompt: Zara has read 60% of her book. What percentage of the book does she still have to read?
explanation: The whole book is 100%, so she still has 100% − 60% = 40% to read.

prompt: Which fraction is bigger, 1/6 or 1/9?
explanation: Cutting a whole into 6 parts gives bigger parts than cutting it into 9 parts, so 1/6 is bigger.

prompt: Is 1/3 more or less than 1/2?
explanation: Thirds are smaller than halves, because the whole is cut into more parts. So 1/3 is less than 1/2.

prompt: Which list of unit fractions is in order from smallest to largest?
explanation: For unit fractions, the bigger the denominator, the smaller the piece. So 1/8 is smallest, then 1/5, then 1/2.

prompt: Which of these fractions is closest to 0 on a number line?
explanation: 1/10 is the smallest of these unit fractions, so it sits closest to 0.

prompt: Which mixed numeral is the same as 7/4?
explanation: 4 quarters make 1 whole, and 7 − 4 = 3 quarters are left over, so 7/4 = 1 3/4.

prompt: Fill the gap: 2 1/3 = ___/3
explanation: Each whole is 3 thirds, so 2 wholes are 6 thirds. Add the 1 third to get 7/3.

prompt: Which improper fraction is equal to 3 2/5?
explanation: 3 wholes are 15 fifths. Add 2 more fifths to get 17/5.

prompt: Fill the gap: 3/4 = ___/8
explanation: 8 is double 4, so double the top number too: 3 × 2 = 6. So 3/4 = 6/8.

prompt: Which list puts 3/4, 5/8 and 1/2 in order from smallest to largest?
explanation: In eighths: 1/2 = 4/8, 5/8 stays 5/8, and 3/4 = 6/8. So the order is 1/2, 5/8, 3/4.

prompt: Ella had 2 litres of water. She drank 3/4 of a litre in the morning and 3/4 of a litre in the afternoon. How many litres of water are left?
explanation: She drank 3/4 + 3/4 = 6/4 = 1 1/2 litres. 2 − 1 1/2 = 1/2 litre is left.

prompt: What is 1/5 of 35?
explanation: To find 1/5, divide by 5: 35 ÷ 5 = 7.

prompt: A bag of potatoes has a mass of 20 kg. What is 1/4 of its mass, in kilograms?
explanation: To find 1/4, divide by 4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 kg.

prompt: What is 1/4 of 10 metres? Give your answer in metres as a decimal.
explanation: 10 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 2, and the 2 left over shared into 4 is 0.5 each. So 1/4 of 10 m is 2.5 m.

prompt: Ruby has $18. She spends 1/4 of it at the school canteen. How many dollars does she spend?
explanation: 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2, and $2 shared into 4 is 50c each. So she spends $4.50.
6 × 4 = 24, and 6 × 4 hundreds = 24 hundreds, which is 2400.

prompt: Which is the best estimate for 38 × 6?

prompt: The canteen sells 1275 pies each term. How many pies does it sell in 4 terms?

prompt: A Sydney ferry makes 24 trips each day. Each trip carries 135 people. How many people does it carry in one day?
What is 47 ÷ 6?

prompt: What is the remainder when 29 is divided by 4?
explanation: 4 × 7 = 28, and 29 − 28 = 1, so the remainder is 1.

prompt: In 58 ÷ 7 = 8 remainder 2, which number is the quotient?
explanation: The quotient is the answer to a division, so it is 8. The divisor is 7, the number we divide by.

prompt: Jai did a division and got 9 remainder 3. The divisor was 5. What number did he divide?
explanation: Check by multiplying and adding: 9 × 5 = 45, then 45 + 3 = 48. So Jai worked out 48 ÷ 5.

prompt: Which is the best estimate for 412 ÷ 8?
explanation: 412 is close to 400, and 400 ÷ 8 = 50. So the answer is about 50.

prompt: 140 students are going to camp. Each tent sleeps 6 students. How many tents are needed so every student has a place?
explanation: 140 ÷ 6 = 23 remainder 2. 23 tents hold 138 students, so 1 more tent is needed for the last 2 students: 24 tents.

prompt: Fill the gap: ___ × 6 = 72
explanation: Use the inverse: 72 ÷ 6 = 12. Check: 12 × 6 = 72.

prompt: Fill the gap: 63 ÷ ___ = 7
explanation: Think of the fact family: 7 × 9 = 63, so 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

prompt: Which multiplication can you use to check that 96 ÷ 8 = 12?
explanation: Multiplication undoes division: if 96 ÷ 8 = 12, then 12 × 8 should give 96, and it does.

prompt: Fill the gap: 36 ÷ 4 = 72 ÷ ___
explanation: 36 ÷ 4 = 9. 72 is double 36, so the divisor must be doubled too: 72 ÷ 8 = 9.

prompt: Ava had $85. She spent $27 on a book and $15 on lunch. How many dollars does she have left?

Line up the place values: 1250 + 375 = 1625, then 1625 + 46 = 1671.

prompt: There were 230 people at the beach. Then 85 more people came and 40 people went home. How many people are at the beach now?
explanation: 230 + 85 = 315 people, then 315 − 40 = 275 people.

prompt: A school fundraiser raised $1245 on Friday and $2380 on Saturday. The goal is $5000. How many more dollars are needed to reach the goal?
explanation: Friday and Saturday together: $1245 + $2380 = $3625. Then $5000 − $3625 = $1375 more is needed.

prompt: How many metres are in 3 kilometres?
Which unit is best for measuring the distance from Sydney to Newcastle?
explanation: Long distances between towns are measured in kilometres. Sydney to Newcastle is about 160 km.

prompt: Write 2450 metres in kilometres.
explanation: 1000 m = 1 km, so divide by 1000: 2450 m = 2.45 km.

prompt: Maya ran 1.5 km on Monday and 800 m on Tuesday. How many metres did she run altogether?
explanation: Change to the same unit first: 1.5 km = 1500 m. Then 1500 m + 800 m = 2300 m.

prompt: A rectangle is 9 cm long and 6 cm wide. What is its perimeter in centimetres?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 165" width="300" height="165" style="max-width:100%;height:auto" fill="currentColor" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14"><rect x="40" y="20" width="200" height="110" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".08" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><text x="140" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16">9 cm</text><text x="250" y="80" font-size="16">6 cm</text></svg>
explanation: Add one length and one width, then double: 9 + 6 = 15, and 15 × 2 = 30 cm.

prompt: A square has sides of 7 m. What is its perimeter in metres?
explanation: A square has 4 equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 × 7 = 28 m.

prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. It is 9 cm long. How wide is it, in centimetres?
explanation: The two lengths use 9 + 9 = 18 cm. That leaves 30 − 18 = 12 cm for the two widths, so each width is 6 cm.

prompt: This L-shaped garden has all right-angled corners. The bottom side is 10 m, the left side is 8 m, the top side is 4 m and the short right side is 3 m. What is its perimeter in metres?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" width="300" height="220" style="max-width:100%;height:auto" fill="currentColor" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14"><polygon points="50,190 250,190 250,130 130,130 130,30 50,30" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".08" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="210" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15">10 m</text><text x="44" y="115" text-anchor="end" font-size="15">8 m</text><text x="90" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15">4 m</text><text x="258" y="165" font-size="15">3 m</text></svg>
explanation: The two missing sides are 8 − 3 = 5 m and 10 − 4 = 6 m. The perimeter is 10 + 8 + 4 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 36 m.

prompt: This rectangle is 6 squares long and 4 squares wide. Each square is 1 square centimetre. What is its area in square centimetres?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 188 132" width="260" height="183" style="max-width:100%;height:auto" fill="currentColor" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14"><rect x="10" y="10" width="168" height="112" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".12"/><path d="M10 10V122M38 10V122M66 10V122M94 10V122M122 10V122M150 10V122M178 10V122M10 10H178M10 38H178M10 66H178M10 94H178M10 122H178" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/></svg>
explanation: There are 4 rows with 6 squares in each row, so the area is 4 × 6 = 24 cm².

prompt: A rectangle is 9 m long and 5 m wide. What is its area in square metres?
explanation: Area = length × width = 9 × 5 = 45 m².

prompt: A rectangle is 2 m long and 50 cm wide. Which calculation gives its area in square centimetres?
explanation: Both sides must use the same unit. 2 m = 200 cm, so the area is 200 × 50 = 10 000 cm².

prompt: A rectangular vegetable patch has an area of 48 square metres. It is 8 m long. How wide is it, in metres?
explanation: Length × width = area, so 8 × ? = 48. 48 ÷ 8 = 6 m.

prompt: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a truck?
explanation: A truck is very heavy, so we use tonnes. 1 tonne = 1000 kg.

prompt: Which unit is best for measuring the amount of medicine in a small spoon?
explanation: A spoon holds only a small amount of liquid, so we use millilitres. A teaspoon holds about 5 mL.

prompt: Which is the most sensible mass for a loaf of bread?
explanation: A loaf of bread is a bit less than 1 kg, so 700 g makes sense. 7 g is like a few sultanas, and 70 kg is like a grown-up.

prompt: Which is the best thing to use to measure 250 mL of milk for a recipe?

choices.text: A measuring jug marked every 50 mL

explanation: A measuring jug measures capacity, and marks every 50 mL let you find 250 mL exactly.

prompt: Which is 3:45 pm in 24-hour time?
explanation: For pm times, add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15, so 3:45 pm is 15:45.

prompt: What is 07:20 in 12-hour time?
explanation: Hours from 00 to 11 are in the morning, so 07:20 is 7:20 am.

prompt: A flight leaves at 21:10. What time is that in 12-hour time?
explanation: 21 is more than 12, so it is pm. 21 − 12 = 9, so 21:10 is 9:10 pm.

prompt: What is 00:15 in 12-hour time?
explanation: 00 is the hour just after midnight, and 12-hour time calls it 12 am. So 00:15 is 12:15 am, a quarter past midnight.

prompt: The angle sits on a protractor. One arm points to 0°. The small marks are every 10°. How many degrees is the angle?

explanation: The second arm is one mark past 120°, so the angle is 120° + 10° = 130°.

prompt: How many degrees are in a right angle?
explanation: A right angle is a quarter turn, which is 90°. A straight angle is 180° and a full turn is 360°.

prompt: An angle measures 125°. What type of angle is it?
explanation: 125° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is an obtuse angle.

prompt: An angle measures 250°. What type of angle is it?
explanation: 250° is more than a straight angle (180°) but less than a full turn (360°), so it is a reflex angle.

prompt: What are the coordinates of point T?

explanation: The origin is where the two axes meet, at 0 across and 0 up: (0, 0).

prompt: Point M is at (2, 3). It moves 4 units to the right and 2 units up. Where is it now?
explanation: Moving right changes the first number: 2 + 4 = 6. Moving up changes the second number: 3 + 2 = 5. So M is now at (6, 5).

prompt: A shape is translated, reflected or rotated. What always stays the same?

choices.text: Its size, but not its shape

explanation: Translations, reflections and rotations only change where a shape is or which way it faces. Its size and shape stay the same.

prompt: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. What type of triangle is it?
explanation: Two sides are the same length (5 cm and 5 cm), so it is an isosceles triangle.

prompt: A triangle has one angle of 90°. What type of triangle is it?
explanation: A triangle with a 90° angle is a right-angled triangle.

prompt: A triangle has angles of 30°, 40° and 110°. What type of triangle is it?
explanation: One angle, 110°, is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse-angled triangle.

prompt: Which of these is a regular polygon?

choices.text: A rectangle 6 cm long and 3 cm wide
A rhombus with angles of 60° and 120°
A triangle with sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm
A hexagon with all sides 4 cm and all angles 120°

explanation: A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal. Only the hexagon has both. The rhombus has equal sides but not equal angles.
verify: 'A hexagon with all sides 4 cm and all angles 120°'

prompt: This net is made of 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. What object does it fold into?

explanation: The 2 triangles are the ends and the 3 rectangles join them, so it folds into a triangular prism.

explanation: The square is the base and the 4 triangles fold up to meet at a point, so it makes a square pyramid.

prompt: Which set of shapes makes the net of a pentagonal prism?
explanation: A prism has 2 matching ends, here pentagons. A pentagon has 5 sides, so 5 rectangles join the ends. 1 pentagon and 5 triangles would make a pentagonal pyramid.

prompt: This square pyramid sits on its square base. What do you see when you look at it from directly above?

choices.text: A square with lines from each corner to the centre
A rectangle with one line across the middle

prompt: An object looks like a triangle from the front and from the side, and like a square from the top. What is it?
explanation: A square top view means a square base, and triangles from the front and side mean the faces slope up to a point. That is a square pyramid.

prompt: An object stands on a triangular face. It looks like a rectangle from the front and from the side, and like a triangle from the top. What is it?
explanation: Seeing a triangle from the top means the object has the same triangle all the way down, standing on its end. Its rectangular faces show from the front and side, so it is a triangular prism.

prompt: What is the mode of this data? 4, 7, 3, 7, 9, 4, 7, 2
say: What is the mode of this data? 4, 7, 3, 7, 9, 4, 7, 2.
explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 7 appears 3 times, more than any other number.

prompt: A class voted for their favourite fruit: apple 6 votes, banana 9 votes, mango 11 votes and orange 4 votes. Which fruit is the mode?
explanation: The mode is the most common answer. Mango has the most votes, 11.

prompt: Four classes collected 40, 80, 120 and 100 cans for recycling. Which scale is most sensible for the vertical axis of a column graph?

prompt: On a column graph the scale goes up in 10s. The column for Year 5 stops exactly halfway between 40 and 50. How many cans did Year 5 collect?
explanation: Halfway between 40 and 50 is 45, so Year 5 collected 45 cans.

prompt: A normal dice has faces numbered 1 to 6. It is rolled once. How many different outcomes are possible?
explanation: The dice can land on 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6, so there are 6 possible outcomes.

prompt: A fair coin is flipped. Are heads and tails equally likely?
explanation: A fair coin has two sides and each is just as likely to land face up, so heads and tails are equally likely.

prompt: This spinner is half red, one quarter blue and one quarter yellow. Are the three colours equally likely?

prompt: A bag has 3 red, 3 blue and 3 green marbles. One marble is taken out without looking. Which of these is true?
explanation: There are the same number of marbles of each colour (3), so each colour is equally likely to be taken.

prompt: Ben spun a spinner 20 times. He got red 9 times, blue 7 times and green the rest of the time. How many times did he get green?
explanation: The frequencies must add to 20. 9 + 7 = 16, so green came up 20 − 16 = 4 times.

prompt: Lucy rolled a dice 30 times. Her results were: 1 came up 4 times, 2 came up 6 times, 3 came up 5 times, 4 came up 3 times, 5 came up 7 times and 6 came up 5 times. Which number came up most often?
explanation: The highest frequency is 7 times, and that was for the number 5. The 7 is how often, not the number rolled.

prompt: A bag has red and blue counters. Mai takes one without looking, writes down the colour and puts it back. She does this 50 times and gets red 38 times and blue 12 times. What is the best conclusion?

choices.text: There are probably more red counters than blue counters in the bag
There are exactly 38 red counters in the bag

There are the same number of red and blue counters

explanation: Red came up much more often, so red is probably more likely, which suggests there are more red counters. The results cannot tell us the exact number.
verify: 'There are probably more red counters than blue counters in the bag'

prompt: A fair coin is flipped 10 times and lands on heads 7 times. Which of these is true about the next flip?

verify: 'Heads and tails are still equally likely'

prompt: At 5 am in Canberra the temperature was −4 °C. By 2 pm it was 13 °C. By how many degrees did the temperature rise?
explanation: From −4 up to 0 is 4 degrees, and from 0 up to 13 is 13 more, so the rise is 4 + 13 = 17 degrees.

prompt: At 4 am the temperature at Perisher was −6 °C. It rose 3 degrees each hour for 4 hours, then fell 5 degrees. What was the temperature then, in °C?
explanation: It rose 3 × 4 = 12 degrees, so −6 + 12 = 6 °C. Then it fell 5 degrees: 6 − 5 = 1 °C.

prompt: Which of these numbers is prime?
explanation: 29 has only two factors, 1 and 29, so it is prime. 21 = 3 × 7, 27 = 3 × 9 and 33 = 3 × 11 are composite.

prompt: Which number between 50 and 70 is a square number?
explanation: The square numbers near there are 7 × 7 = 49, 8 × 8 = 64 and 9 × 9 = 81. Only 64 is between 50 and 70.

prompt: Why is the number 1 neither prime nor composite?

choices.text: Because it is an odd number
Because it has exactly one factor
Because it has exactly two factors
Because every number divides into it

explanation: A prime has exactly two factors and a composite number has more than two. The number 1 has only one factor (itself), so it is neither.

prompt: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 40?
explanation: The primes between 20 and 40 are 23, 29, 31 and 37. That is 4 primes; numbers like 21, 27 and 39 are multiples of 3.

prompt: Work out 3.45 + 2.7

prompt: Work out 0.6 × 30
explanation: 0.6 × 3 = 1.8, and then × 10 gives 18.

prompt: A school buys 300 rulers at $0.45 each and 20 glue sticks at $1.25 each. What is the total cost in dollars?

Without working it out exactly, which is the answer to 8 × 4.95?
explanation: 4.95 is close to 5, and 8 × 5 = 40, so the answer must be about 40. That is 39.6.

prompt: Mangoes cost $2.35 each. Priya buys 7 mangoes and pays with a $20 note. How much change does she get, in dollars?
Work out 3 + 4 × 5
explanation: Multiply before adding: 4 × 5 = 20, then 3 + 20 = 23.

prompt: Work out (7 + 5) × 3
explanation: Brackets first: 7 + 5 = 12, then 12 × 3 = 36.

prompt: Work out 48 ÷ 6 − 2 × 3
explanation: Do the division and multiplication first: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 2 × 3 = 6. Then 8 − 6 = 2.

prompt: Where do brackets go to make this number sentence true? 6 + 4 × 5 − 2 = 30
What number goes in the gap? 3 × ___ + 4 = 19
explanation: Take away the 4 first: 19 − 4 = 15. Then 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Check: 3 × 5 + 4 = 19.

prompt: What number goes in the gap? 4 × ___ − 2 = 26
Mr Nguyen has 4 full packs of pencils and 3 loose pencils. He has 39 pencils altogether. How many pencils are in each pack?
explanation: Without the 3 loose pencils there are 39 − 3 = 36 in the packs, and 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

prompt: What number goes in the gap? (___ − 4) ÷ 3 + 2 = 7
A growing pattern has these terms. Position 1: 4, position 2: 7, position 3: 10, position 4: 13. What is the term at position 5?
explanation: The terms go up by 3 each time, so the next term is 13 + 3 = 16.

prompt: A pattern has terms 5, 9, 13, 17 at positions 1, 2, 3, 4. Which rule gives the term from its position number?

choices.text: Multiply the position number by 4, then add 1

verify: 'Multiply the position number by 4, then add 1'

prompt: The rule for a pattern is 'multiply the position number by 3, then add 1'. Position 1 is 4, position 2 is 7 and position 3 is 10. What is the term at position 20?
A decimal pattern starts 0.5, 0.8, 1.1, 1.4, … and keeps going the same way. The first term is at position 1. What is the term at position 10?
explanation: The pattern goes up by 0.3 each time. From position 1 to position 10 is 9 steps, so 0.5 + 9 × 0.3 = 0.5 + 2.7 = 3.2.

prompt: Bananas cost $3.50 per kilogram. How much do 4 kg of bananas cost, in dollars?
A car travels 240 km in 3 hours at a steady speed. How many kilometres does it travel each hour?
explanation: Share the distance by the hours: 240 ÷ 3 = 80 km each hour.

prompt: A 5 kg bag of potatoes costs $8.50. What is the cost per kilogram, in dollars?
explanation: Divide the cost by the mass: $8.50 ÷ 5 = $1.70 per kilogram.

prompt: Which bottle of milk is the best buy (the cheapest per litre)?
explanation: Find the price of 1 L in each: $1.70, $3.20 ÷ 2 = $1.60, $4.50 ÷ 3 = $1.50 and $6.40 ÷ 4 = $1.60. The 3 L bottle is cheapest per litre.

prompt: What number goes in the gap? 1/2 = ___/10
explanation: Ten is 5 times 2, so the top number is 5 times 1: 1/2 = 5/10.

prompt: What is 6/8 written in simplest form?
explanation: Divide the top and bottom by 2, their highest common factor: 6/8 = 3/4.

prompt: The rectangle is split into 12 equal parts and 8 are shaded. What fraction is shaded, in simplest form?
explanation: 8/12 shaded. Divide the top and bottom by 4: 8/12 = 2/3. You can also see 2 of the 3 rows are shaded.

prompt: Which is 36/48 written in simplest form?
explanation: The highest common factor of 36 and 48 is 12: 36 ÷ 12 = 3 and 48 ÷ 12 = 4, so 36/48 = 3/4. The others are equivalent but can still be simplified.

prompt: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
explanation: When the top number is 1, a bigger bottom number means smaller pieces. So 1/4 < 1/3 < 1/2.

prompt: This number line from 0 to 1 is split into equal parts. Which fraction is at point P?
explanation: The line is split into 6 equal parts and P is 4 parts along, so P is at 4/6, which is 2/3.

prompt: Which fraction is between 1/2 and 3/4 on a number line?
explanation: Using twelfths: 1/2 = 6/12, 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12, so 2/3 is between them.

prompt: Which list puts 5/8, 2/3 and 3/5 in order from smallest to largest?
Work out 1/2 + 3/8
explanation: Change 1/2 into eighths: 4/8 + 3/8 = 7/8.

prompt: Work out 5/6 − 1/3
explanation: Change 1/3 into sixths: 5/6 − 2/6 = 3/6, which is 1/2.

prompt: A cake recipe needs 3/4 cup of flour for the cake and 5/8 cup of flour for the icing. How many cups of flour is that altogether?
explanation: Change 3/4 into eighths: 6/8 + 5/8 = 11/8, which is 1 3/8 cups.

prompt: Noah had 2 1/4 m of rope. He cut off 5/8 m, and then another 3/4 m. How many metres of rope were left?
Which fraction is the same as 3 ÷ 4?
explanation: A division can be written as a fraction: 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4.

prompt: 5 children share 2 sandwiches equally. What fraction of a sandwich does each child get?
explanation: 2 shared among 5 is 2 ÷ 5 = 2/5 of a sandwich each.

prompt: Work out 17 ÷ 5. Write the whole answer as a mixed numeral, such as 2 1/3.
explanation: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2, and the 2 left over is shared by 5, so the answer is 3 2/5 (which is 3.4).

prompt: At table A, 4 children share 3 pizzas equally. At table B, 6 children share 5 pizzas equally. Which is true?

choices.text: Each child at table A gets more
Each child at table B gets more
Every child gets the same amount
Each child gets 1/4 of a pizza

explanation: Table A: 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4 = 9/12 each. Table B: 5 ÷ 6 = 5/6 = 10/12 each. So each child at table B gets more.
verify: 'Each child at table B gets more'

prompt: What is 2/3 of 24?
explanation: One third of 24 is 24 ÷ 3 = 8, so two thirds is 2 × 8 = 16.

prompt: What is 3/4 of 20?
explanation: One quarter of 20 is 5, so three quarters is 3 × 5 = 15.

prompt: 3/5 of a number is 12. What is the number?
explanation: If 3 fifths is 12, then 1 fifth is 12 ÷ 3 = 4, and 5 fifths is 5 × 4 = 20.

prompt: Lily had $60. She spent 1/4 of it on a book. Then she spent 2/3 of the money that was left on a cricket ball. How much money does she have now, in dollars?
explanation: The book cost 1/4 of $60 = $15, leaving $45. The ball cost 2/3 of $45 = $30, so she has $45 − $30 = $15.

prompt: What is 10% of 350?
explanation: 10% means one tenth, so divide by 10: 350 ÷ 10 = 35.

prompt: What is 25% of 80?
explanation: 25% is one quarter, and 80 ÷ 4 = 20.

prompt: What is 30% of 60?
A footy club has 240 members. 35% of them are juniors. How many members are NOT juniors?
explanation: 10% of 240 is 24 and 5% is 12, so 35% is 24 + 24 + 24 + 12 = 84 juniors. That leaves 240 − 84 = 156 members.

prompt: A pair of runners costs $80. In a sale they have 50% off. What is the sale price, in dollars?
explanation: 50% off takes off half: half of $80 is $40, so the sale price is $80 − $40 = $40.

prompt: A cricket bat costs $60. It has 10% off. How many dollars is the discount?
A jacket costs $79.95. It has 30% off. Which is the best estimate of the sale price?
explanation: $79.95 is about $80. 30% of $80 is $24, so the sale price is about $80 − $24 = $56.

prompt: Shop A sells a scooter for $120 with 25% off. Shop B sells the same scooter for $95 with 10% off. How many dollars cheaper is the cheaper shop?
explanation: Shop A: 25% of $120 is $30, so $90. Shop B: 10% of $95 is $9.50, so $85.50. Shop B is $90 − $85.50 = $4.50 cheaper.

prompt: At a Bunnings sausage sizzle, a sausage sandwich costs $3.50 and a drink costs $2. Ava buys 3 sandwiches and 2 drinks and pays with a $20 note. How much change does she get, in dollars?
explanation: 3 sandwiches cost $10.50 and 2 drinks cost $4, so she spends $14.50. Her change is $20 − $14.50 = $5.50.

prompt: Tom buys a pie for $4.80 and a juice for $2.65. How much does he spend, in dollars?
Mia buys items costing $4.95, $3.10 and $6.90. Which is the best estimate of the total?
explanation: Round each price: $5 + $3 + $7 = $15. (The exact total is $14.95.)

prompt: Movie tickets cost $18.50 for an adult and $12.50 for a child. The Patel family buys 2 adult and 3 child tickets and uses a voucher for 20% off the total. How much do they pay, in dollars?
How many metres are in 2.5 km?
Write 750 g in kilograms.
Which of these lengths is the longest?
explanation: Change them all to metres: 1.2 m, 125 cm = 1.25 m, 1050 mm = 1.05 m and 0.9 m. The longest is 125 cm.

prompt: A jug holds 1.5 L of juice. Ben pours 4 glasses of 250 mL each and then 1 glass of 180 mL. How many millilitres of juice are left in the jug?
explanation: 1.5 L = 1500 mL. He pours 4 × 250 = 1000 mL and then 180 mL, so 1500 − 1000 − 180 = 320 mL are left.

prompt: A rectangle has an area of 48 cm² and a width of 6 cm. How long is it, in centimetres?
explanation: Area = length × width, so the length is 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm.

prompt: A rectangular garden bed is 7 m long and 3 m wide. What is its area, in square metres?
explanation: Area = length × width = 7 × 3 = 21 m².

prompt: All of these rectangles have a perimeter of 20 cm. Which one has the largest area?
explanation: The areas are 9, 16, 24 and 25 cm². The 5 cm by 5 cm square has the largest area.

prompt: A rectangle has an area of 36 cm² and a perimeter of 26 cm. How long is its longer side, in centimetres?
explanation: Try sides that multiply to 36: 4 cm by 9 cm has perimeter 4 + 9 + 4 + 9 = 26 cm. So the longer side is 9 cm.

prompt: This L-shape is made from rectangles. It is 10 cm along the bottom and 8 cm up the left side. The top edge is 4 cm and the right edge is 3 cm. What is its area, in square centimetres?
explanation: Split it into a 4 cm by 8 cm rectangle (32 cm²) and a 6 cm by 3 cm rectangle (18 cm²). 32 + 18 = 50 cm².

explanation: The whole lawn is 12 × 9 = 108 m². Take away the pond, 4 × 3 = 12 m²: 108 − 12 = 96 m².

explanation: Top bar: 12 × 3 = 36 cm². Stem: 4 × 6 = 24 cm². Total: 36 + 24 = 60 cm².

explanation: With the path, the outside is 14 m by 10 m = 140 m². Take away the pool, 10 × 6 = 60 m²: 140 − 60 = 80 m².

explanation: Area of a parallelogram = base × perpendicular height = 8 × 5 = 40 cm². The slanted side is not needed.

explanation: Area of a triangle = half of base × height = half of 10 × 6 = half of 60 = 30 cm².

prompt: Why is the area of a triangle half of base × height?

choices.text: Two copies of the triangle fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and height
A triangle has 3 sides and a rectangle has 4 sides
The height of a triangle is always half of its base
Every triangle is half of a square

explanation: Two identical triangles make a parallelogram with area base × height, so one triangle is half of that.
verify: 'Two copies of the triangle fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and height'

prompt: A triangle has an area of 24 cm² and a base of 8 cm. What is its perpendicular height, in centimetres?
explanation: Half of base × height = 24, so base × height = 48. Then height = 48 ÷ 8 = 6 cm.

prompt: 1 hectare = 10 000 m². How many square metres are in 3 hectares?
explanation: Each hectare is 10 000 m², so 3 ha = 3 × 10 000 = 30 000 m².

prompt: Which unit is best for measuring the area of a national park?
explanation: A national park is huge, so square kilometres (km²) are the sensible unit.

prompt: A rectangular paddock is 200 m long and 100 m wide. What is its area in hectares? (1 ha = 10 000 m²)
A rectangular field is 400 m long and 250 m wide. A farmer plants wheat on half of the field. How many hectares of wheat are planted? (1 ha = 10 000 m²)
explanation: The field is 400 × 250 = 100 000 m², which is 10 ha. Half of 10 ha is 5 ha.

prompt: A box is 5 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high. What is its volume, in cubic centimetres?
explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cm³.

prompt: A rectangular prism is built from centimetre cubes. Each layer has 4 rows of 6 cubes, and there are 2 layers. How many cubes are used?
explanation: One layer has 4 × 6 = 24 cubes, and 2 layers have 2 × 24 = 48 cubes.

prompt: Which box has the same volume as a box 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 2 cm high?
explanation: 6 × 4 × 2 = 48 cm³ and 8 × 3 × 2 = 48 cm³. The others are 72, 24 and 60 cm³.

prompt: A fish tank is 20 cm long and 10 cm wide and has some water in it. When a rock is put in, the water level rises by 3 cm. What is the volume of the rock, in cubic centimetres?
explanation: The rock pushes up a layer of water 20 cm by 10 cm by 3 cm, so its volume is 20 × 10 × 3 = 600 cm³.

prompt: A bus leaves Hornsby at 8:47 am and arrives at Chatswood at 9:22 am. How many minutes does the trip take?
explanation: From 8:47 to 9:00 is 13 minutes, and from 9:00 to 9:22 is 22 minutes. 13 + 22 = 35 minutes.

prompt: What is 3:45 pm in 24-hour time?
explanation: For pm times after 1 pm, add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15, so 3:45 pm is 15:45.

prompt: Use the train timetable. How many minutes does the train take to go from Strathfield to Penrith?
explanation: Strathfield 14:19 to 15:00 is 41 minutes, and 15:00 to 15:12 is 12 minutes. 41 + 12 = 53 minutes.

prompt: A movie starts at 7:50 pm and runs for 2 hours 25 minutes. Mila's mum picks her up 20 minutes after it ends. What is the pick-up time in 24-hour time?
explanation: 7:50 pm + 2 h = 9:50 pm, + 25 min = 10:15 pm, + 20 min = 10:35 pm. In 24-hour time that is 22:35.

prompt: The angles marked 130° and a are next to each other on a straight line. What is the size of angle a, in degrees?
explanation: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, so a = 180° − 130° = 50°.

explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so b = 65°.

prompt: Start at the origin (0, 0). Move 4 units left and 1 unit down. What are the coordinates of the point you reach?
explanation: Left makes x negative and down makes y negative, so the point is (−4, −1). The x-coordinate is written first.

prompt: Point P is at (2, 5). It is moved 6 units left and 3 units down. What are its new coordinates?
explanation: Left 6 changes x: 2 − 6 = −4. Down 3 changes y: 5 − 3 = 2. The new point is (−4, 2).

prompt: Point Q is at (−3, 4). It moves 5 units to the right and then 6 units down. What are its new coordinates?
explanation: Moving right adds 5 to the x-coordinate: −3 + 5 = 2. Moving down takes 6 from the y-coordinate: 4 − 6 = −2.

prompt: A solid has a hexagon for its base and triangle faces that meet at one point at the top. What is it called?
explanation: Triangle faces meeting at a point make a pyramid, and it is named after its base, so it is a hexagonal pyramid.

prompt: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
explanation: It has 2 triangle faces (the ends) and 3 rectangle faces, so 5 faces.

prompt: A hexagonal prism is cut straight through, parallel to its end faces. What shape is the cut face (the cross-section)?
explanation: A cross-section of a prism cut parallel to its ends is the same shape as the ends, so it is a hexagon.

prompt: A prism has 18 edges. How many vertices does it have?
explanation: A prism with an n-sided base has 3n edges, so 3n = 18 and n = 6 (a hexagonal prism). It has 2 × 6 = 12 vertices.

prompt: Which of these shapes will NOT tessellate on its own?
explanation: Squares, equilateral triangles and regular hexagons fit together with no gaps. Regular pentagons always leave gaps.

prompt: Tiles in a pattern are made by sliding the same shape along, without turning or flipping it. Which transformation is that?
explanation: Sliding a shape without turning or flipping it is called a translation.

prompt: Each angle of a regular hexagon is 120°. Why do regular hexagons tessellate?

choices.text: Because three 120° angles fit exactly around a point to make 360°
Because all their sides are the same length
Because they have lines of symmetry

explanation: Where hexagons meet, three corners of 120° fill the whole 360° around the point, so there are no gaps.
verify: 'Because three 120° angles fit exactly around a point to make 360°'

prompt: Each angle of a regular octagon is 135°. Why won't regular octagons tessellate on their own?

choices.text: Because 360° cannot be made from 135° angles, so there is always a gap or an overlap at a point
Because octagons have an even number of sides
Because octagons have no lines of symmetry

explanation: Two octagon corners make 270° and three make 405°. Neither is 360°, so they leave a gap or overlap.
verify: 'Because 360° cannot be made from 135° angles, so there is always a gap or an overlap at a point'

prompt: A cricketer scored these runs: 12, 45, 7, 30, 45, 18. What is the range of the scores?
explanation: Range = highest − lowest = 45 − 7 = 38.

prompt: What is the mode of these shoe sizes? 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 6, 7, 9
explanation: The mode is the most common value. Size 6 appears 3 times, more than any other size.

prompt: Five test scores have a range of 20. The lowest score is 63. What is the highest score?
explanation: Range = highest − lowest, so highest = 63 + 20 = 83.

prompt: Daily top temperatures (°C) for a week. Town A: 24, 25, 25, 26, 25, 24, 26. Town B: 18, 31, 25, 22, 29, 25, 20. Which statement is true?

choices.text: Town A has a larger range than Town B
The two towns have different modes
Both towns have a mode of 25 °C, but Town B's temperatures are more spread out
Both towns have the same range

explanation: Both modes are 25 °C. Town A's range is 26 − 24 = 2 and Town B's range is 31 − 18 = 13, so Town B is more spread out.
verify: "Both towns have a mode of 25 °C, but Town B's temperatures are more spread out"

prompt: An advertisement says '4 out of 5 dentists recommend Brite-Smile toothpaste'. Only 5 dentists were asked, and all of them work for the Brite-Smile company. What is the best criticism of the claim?

choices.text: 4 out of 5 is less than half
Dentists do not know about toothpaste
The sample is very small, and the dentists may be biased because they work for the company

explanation: Five dentists is a tiny sample, and people who work for the company are not a fair group to ask.
verify: 'The sample is very small, and the dentists may be biased because they work for the company'

prompt: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green marbles. One marble is picked without looking. What is the probability it is blue? Write it as a fraction.
explanation: There are 10 marbles and 5 are blue, so the probability is 5/10, which is 1/2.

prompt: A normal dice is numbered 1 to 6. Which event has a probability of 0?
explanation: There is no 7 on the dice, so rolling a 7 is impossible: its probability is 0. Rolling a number less than 7 is certain (probability 1).

prompt: The probability that it will rain tomorrow is 0.35. What is the probability that it will NOT rain tomorrow?
explanation: The probabilities of all outcomes add to 1, so 1 − 0.35 = 0.65.

prompt: A spinner has 8 equal sections. Which spinner gives red a probability of 1/4, blue a probability of 1/2, and green the rest?
explanation: 1/4 of 8 is 2 red and 1/2 of 8 is 4 blue. That leaves 8 − 2 − 4 = 2 green.

prompt: A spinner has 5 equal sections and 2 of them are blue. It is spun 100 times. How many times would you expect it to land on blue?
explanation: The probability of blue is 2/5, and 2/5 of 100 is 40.

prompt: A fair coin is tossed 50 times. About how many heads would you expect?
explanation: Heads has a probability of 1/2, and half of 50 is 25.

prompt: Jai rolls a fair dice 30 times. He expects about 5 sixes but gets 4. Which statement is true?

choices.text: The dice must be unfair because he did not get exactly 5
Getting 4 instead of 5 is normal, because results vary from what is expected
His next roll is more likely to be a six

explanation: Expected results are a guide, not a promise. Small differences like 4 instead of 5 happen all the time with a fair dice.
verify: 'Getting 4 instead of 5 is normal, because results vary from what is expected'

prompt: A spinner has 4 equal sections and 1 is red. Sara spins it 20 times and gets red 9 times. What is most likely if she spins it 1000 times?

choices.text: About 450 reds, because she got 9 reds in 20 spins
About 250 reds, because results get closer to 1/4 with more spins
There is no way to know, because spinners are random

explanation: The probability of red is 1/4, and 1/4 of 1000 is 250. With many more spins, the results usually get close to the expected 250.
verify: 'About 250 reds, because results get closer to 1/4 with more spins'

say: Read these words to a grown-up. A grown-up will mark it.
answer: see, moon, rain, boat, cake, bike, home, feet, tube, play (8 or more read correctly)
explanation: Two vowels together, or a vowel with an e at the end, often make one long sound. Reading 8 or more of the 10 words correctly is a pass.

say: Which box has the word said? said.

prompt: Listen, then type the word you hear.
say: was. It was hot at the beach. was.
explanation: Was is a tricky word. It is spelt w-a-s, even though it sounds like 'woz'.

prompt: Listen, then type the word you hear.
say: into. The frog jumped into the pond. into.
explanation: Into is two small words joined together: in + to.

prompt: Which word fits? I have __ hands.
explanation: Two (t-w-o) is the number 2. You have two hands.

prompt: Which word means more than one cat?
explanation: Adding s to cat makes cats, which means more than one cat.

prompt: Which word fits? Yesterday I __ over the log.
explanation: Yesterday is in the past, so we add -ed: jumped.

prompt: Listen, then type the word you hear.
say: playing. We are playing in the sand. playing.
explanation: Play + ing makes playing. The word play does not change.

prompt: Listen, then type the word you hear.
say: looked. I looked under the bed. looked.
explanation: Look + ed makes looked. The -ed ending can sound like 't', but it is still spelt e-d.

prompt: Which word does not belong?
explanation: Dog, cat and cow are animals. A bus is not an animal.

prompt: Which one is a colour?
explanation: Blue is a colour. A jumper is clothes and bread is food.

prompt: Shirt, sock, hat. What group do these words belong to?
explanation: A shirt, a sock and a hat are all things we wear, so they are clothes.

prompt: Carrot, peas, apple, potato. Which one is not in the same group?
explanation: Carrots, peas and potatoes are vegetables. An apple is a fruit.

prompt: The dog likes to bark. What does bark mean here?

choices.text: the loud sound a dog makes

explanation: A dog barks when it makes a loud woof. Bark can also mean the outside of a tree, but not here.

prompt: I hit the ball with a bat. What is the bat?

choices.text: an animal that flies at night
a stick for hitting a ball

explanation: You hit a ball with a cricket bat, so here a bat is a stick for hitting.

prompt: Mum wears a gold ring. What is the ring?

choices.text: something you wear on a finger

explanation: You wear a ring on your finger. Ring can also mean the sound a phone makes, but you cannot wear a sound.

prompt: In which sentence is a fly a bug?

choices.text: A fly sat on my toast.

explanation: A fly that sits on toast is a small bug. In the other sentences, fly means to move through the air.

prompt: Look at the picture. Where is the ball?
explanation: The ball is below the table top, between the legs, so it is under the table.
